open_issues: search_fts (FTS5 virtual table) has no EF DbSet by design — FTS5 virtual tables have no natural EF Core shape, so it is queried with raw SQL (MATCH) at a higher layer; the table, its content-table link to search_chunks, and its sync triggers are all created by the migration.

OfficialNumberService's numbering-format templating supports only the documented token vocabulary (YYYYMMDD, D, E, SSS) via literal substitution, not a general template engine; sufficient for the default format and any admin-tool-produced format built from the same tokens, but not for arbitrary custom formats.

Wakeel.Crypto is not referenced anywhere in Wakeel.Core, per instructions; the AdminWrap/PasswordWrap/RecoveryWrap key-unwrapping that yields the 32-byte DbKey happens in a higher layer (Wakeel.Crypto/Desktop) — Core only accepts already-derived key bytes.
notes:
Scope: full DATA-MODEL.md §0-12 for the Wakeel database (66 relational tables + the search_fts FTS5 virtual table), matching entity classes in Wakeel.Core.Data.Entities, all wired through one WakeelDb DbContext.

Key design decisions (documented in code comments too):
- SyncedEntity (id/created_at/updated_at/origin_device/row_version/base_version/deleted_at) is applied to every table in DATA-MODEL §2-§10 whose row lists an `id` column (44 tables) — these are the "official" records per §0's shared-prefix convention. Tables in §1 (installation, org_units, devices, account, settings, official_numbers, audit_log, notifications, clock_checks, health_snapshots) and §11-§12 (change_log, sync_packages, sync_conflicts, phone_queue, pairing_sessions, pinned_files, backups, restore_log, search_chunks, models) are local/technical and are plain entities, per the explicit "local tables are not synced" rule and because several of them already define their own distinct timestamp scheme (issued_at/paired_at/checked_at/etc.) rather than created_at/updated_at. document_pages and document_links have no `id` column in DATA-MODEL and use composite keys instead.
- Task entity is named TaskItem (not Task) to avoid colliding with System.Threading.Tasks.Task under ImplicitUsings; models table's entity is SearchModel (mapped to table "models") to avoid the generic name Model. installation/account are singleton rows keyed by a fixed literal "singleton" id (a technical PK, not a DATA-MODEL column) since EF requires a key.
- Schema is plain embedded SQL (Migrations/0001_initial.sql, ~66 CREATE TABLE + indexes + FK constraints for the clear single-parent relationships + 88 change_log AFTER INSERT/UPDATE triggers on every synced table + FTS5 virtual table with 3 sync triggers), applied by SchemaMigrator via a schema_versions tracking table it creates itself; EF's own migration system is not used at all, so the EF model configures no FK/navigation graph — only table names, keys, and value conversions — since referential integrity lives purely in SQL.
- Naming convention: a model-building pass in WakeelDb.OnModelCreating converts every C# property name to its snake_case column name (e.g. OrgId -> org_id) and applies value converters generically by CLR type: enums -> snake_case text (EnumSnakeCaseConverter<T>/NullableEnumSnakeCaseConverter<T>, reflection-selected), DateTime/DateTime? -> ISO-8601 UTC text, Guid PKs -> ValueGeneratedNever (app-generates via Guid.CreateVersion7() in each entity's property initializer). ChangeLogEntry.Op is a dedicated non-generic converter mapping Insert/Update to the literal "I"/"U" the SQL triggers write. IgnoreDeleted() is a one-line wrapper over EF's IgnoreQueryFilters(), applied per the spec's literal method name.
- Found and fixed a real timezone bug during testing (not test-only): DateTime.ParseExact treats an unescaped literal 'Z' in a custom format string as a UTC marker and silently returns Kind=Local with the value shifted by the local UTC offset, even under DateTimeStyles.None. The dev machine's local zone (UTC+3) made this reproduce reliably. Fixed by stripping the trailing 'Z' before ParseExact and parsing the remainder with a Z-free format, then SpecifyKind(Utc) — this affects every DateTime read back from the database, so it was important to catch here.
- DbConnectionFactory disables Microsoft.Data.Sqlite's connection pooling (Pooling=false): pooled native handles retain whatever key unlocked them, so reusing the pool across a wrong-key attempt or a lock/re-key cycle would silently reuse an already-unlocked handle instead of validating the new key — this broke the "wrong key rejected" and "Unlock with wrong key throws" behavior until disabled.
- OfficialNumberService takes an explicit ClockVerdict parameter (computed by ClockCheckService) rather than depending on it directly, keeping the "refuse on bad clock" and "refuse on earlier date" rules both enforced but decoupled — a higher-level orchestration service (outside B0-CORE) is expected to call ClockCheckService then OfficialNumberService together, and to combine numbering with correspondence approval in one transaction as ARCHITECTURE §5 describes; OfficialNumberService.IssueAsync itself is transactional via a single SaveChangesAsync.
- ArabicText.Plural maps count 0 to the `plural` (3-10) form since DATA-MODEL/ARCHITECTURE describe 5 agreement buckets (0,1,2,3-10,11+) but the method signature only supplies 4 strings; `pluralOver10` is the Arabic singular-tamyiz form used from 11 upward (e.g. "11 موظفًا"), distinct from the bare singular used for exactly 1.
- AddWakeelCore registers Clock/IdGenerator/ErrorMapper (stateless) and the DB-backed services (Audit/Settings/OfficialNumber/FinancialCycle/ClockCheck) as Scoped, resolving WakeelDb from the container; it does not itself construct a WakeelDb/DbSession since that requires the account-password-derived 32-byte key, which is only available after login — the host app registers WakeelDb once a DbSession is open.
- Verified the "EF model must match SQL schema exactly" acceptance criterion two ways: (a) a scripted diff confirming the 66 EF ToTable() names equal the 66 SQL CREATE TABLE names exactly, and (b) a test that migrates a fresh temp SQLCipher database and queries every one of WakeelDb's DbSet<> properties (66 of them), asserting each returns an empty result rather than throwing.
